overview: City Council President Zac Bears discussed Medford's budget reforms, infrastructure backlogs, and the need for commercial growth to alleviate residential tax burdens. The interview highlighted upcoming decisions regarding a new high school and strategies to improve public engagement on zoning.

items.title: Introduction and Personal Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced City Council President Zac Bears, who shared his history as a Medford native and his values-based approach to governance.

items.title: Budget Reform and Teacher Contracts
items.summary: Bears highlighted improvements to the budget transparency process and the successful 2024 teacher contract as major recent accomplishments.

items.title: Infrastructure Challenges and Implementation
items.summary: The discussion identified a historical failure to execute city plans, resulting in a significant backlog for road, sidewalk, and sewer repairs.

items.title: Public Engagement and Zoning Reset
items.summary: Bears acknowledged the friction caused by recent zoning discussions and emphasized a need for better communication and mutual respect between the council and residents.

items.title: Commercial Growth and Revenue
items.summary: Bears argued that commercial and mixed-use growth in the squares and corridors is the only sustainable way to lower residential tax bills.

items.title: Housing Crisis and Zoning Strategy
items.summary: The conversation focused on the housing crisis and a vision for becoming a 'City of Yes' regarding property adaptation and bold housing projects.

items.title: Major Infrastructure: Fire Station and High School
items.summary: Bears discussed the missed opportunity for a new fire station and provided an update on the high school building project's design options.

items.title: High School Building Project Costs
items.summary: Bears detailed the potential $700 million to $900 million cost for a new high school, noting that state reimbursement makes it more fiscally responsible than a simple code upgrade.

items.title: Vision for the Future
items.summary: Bears outlined a 15-year vision for Medford featuring thriving business squares, safe streets for all modes of transit, and a proactive mindset toward development.

items.title: Closing Remarks
items.summary: Petrella concluded the interview with information on how citizens can watch the program and contact the show.
